## When to apply
When implementing any feature, fix, or refactor that touches multiple files or locations.

## Steps
1. Break the work into the smallest independently testable changes
2. Make one change at a time - edit one file or one function
3. Verify each change works (compiles, tests pass) before making the next
4. If a change fails, you know exactly which edit caused the problem

## Why this matters
Large multi-file changes without intermediate verification create a debugging nightmare. When something breaks, any of the N changes could be the cause. Small incremental changes give you N independent verification points, each trivial to debug.

## Pitfalls
- Editing 5 files to implement a feature before testing any of them
- Thinking you can hold all the interdependencies in your head without verification
- Skipping the build step for changes that seem obviously correct
description: Make small, testable changes one at a time and verify each before making the next.
